subject: Conditional purchase workflow decision for Procurely trial
message_1_body:
Hi Logan —

Thanks for taking this on. We (Procurely) are gearing up for a 6-week technical pilot with Redwood engineering next week and want to make sure billing and onboarding are aligned. Our legal/finance prefers an invoice-only flow for short trials because our procurement cycle takes 6–8 weeks. Can Redwood accept invoice-only for a limited pilot window and then switch to PO-based procurement for any renewal?

What evidence or onboarding forms do you need from us to qualify? I attached our onboarding form for reference (procurely_onboarding_form.pdf).

High level: pilot cap ~$9,500 total, single invoice after completion, billing contact billing@procurely.com. If there are specific fields that must appear on the invoice or a one-time waiver we should follow, point us to it and we’ll comply.

Appreciate any guidance — happy to hop on a 20 min call with finance if that helps.

Best,
Alex Ramos
Head of Partnerships, Procurely
alex.ramos@procurely.com
message_2_subject: Re: Pilot onboarding / billing path question
message_2_body:
Alex —

Thanks for the details and for attaching the form. Short answer: yes, we can sometimes do an invoice-only path for short, low-risk pilots, but it requires a conditional approval from Finance and a small set of controls so we don’t create an open spend that bypasses PO governance. I’ve looped in Marissa (Finance) and Karthik (Legal/Procure) to confirm specifics.

From experience, what we typically need for a conditional invoice-only pilot: 
- Signed onboarding form (you sent that)
- Signed SLA or terms addendum for the pilot (one-time, limits liability and clarifies billing)
- Evidence: W-9 / tax ID and insurance cert if services cross certain thresholds
- Single-invoice expectation documented (invoice date and total)
- Billing contact and address on file (billing@procurely.com is fine)

If Finance approves, here’s the gating flow I suggest:
1) Procurely returns completed onboarding form + W-9 + signed SLA addendum.
2) Finance issues a one-time conditional waiver that allows the pilot to be invoiced without a PO up to $15,000.
3) Redwood accounting will require invoice to include a reference code we provide and to be emailed to accounting@redwood.com.
4) Any renewal >$15k or ongoing work will need a PO or a contract with purchase terms.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the waiver language and any required invoice fields? If you’re OK, I’ll get Procurely to sign the SLA and route the docs.

Cheers,
Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Fwd: Re: Pilot onboarding / billing path question — conditional approval
message_3_body:
Logan / Karthik —

I reviewed the details and approve a conditional invoice-only path for Procurely’s 6-week pilot with the following mandatory controls: 

1) Pilot cap: not to exceed $15,000 total (we’ll document max value on the waiver).
2) Required docs before provisioning: completed onboarding form, W-9, signed SLA addendum (attached), and SOC2 report or last 12 months of security attestation if available.
3) Invoice requirements: a single invoice after pilot completion, clearly labeled "One-time pilot invoice — DEAL-78921"; include remit-to details; email invoice to accounting@redwood.com and cc marissa.cole@redwood.com.
4) Approval cadence: waiver is valid for this pilot only. Any extension or renewal must follow standard PO/contract process.
5) Finance will hold billing until the warranty/acceptance criteria are met and the engineering lead signs off.

I attached the SLA addendum we require for short pilots (procurely-signed-sla.pdf). Once Procurely returns the completed package I will issue the conditional waiver document and copy accounting for invoicing instructions.

Please confirm if Procurely can return the docs by EOD Monday so we can turn up the trial Tuesday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager — Redwood Inference
